Binding architectural constraints; they override the generic thinking guides below wherever the two conflict. (1) Core stays small - add capability via channels/, tools/, skills, or MCP; keep agent/loop.py and agent/runner.py changes minimal and justified. (2) Less structure, more intelligence - no new framework layer unless it removes real complexity or protects a real boundary. (3) Prefer duplication over premature abstraction - channels and providers MAY repeat send retries, media handling, and message splitting; each file stays self-contained and readable on its own. (4) Minimal change that solves the real problem - do not bundle unrelated refactors into a feature or bugfix.
Apply canonical package/component/action/redaction contracts to every remaining runtime family.
Reuse current channel/provider/hook/CLI owners and delete duplicate lifecycle paths.
Track family state and actions through runtime, Settings, CLI, and frontend compatibility boundaries.
